about: Every IPMA warning above green that we have read, each with the reads that bracket it: first_read_utc (the first of our reads that carried it) and last_read_utc; gone_read_utc is the first read that no longer carried it, and 'gone' says how: ended (its window was over), replaced (a new row for the same area and type overlapping its window appeared in that read: see replaced_by) or withdrawn (nothing took its place). IPMA's feed has no time of issue and no identifier: a changed warning is a new row, so 'replaced' is our pairing by area, type and window, and the true time of the change lies between the two reads (first_last_modified, IPMA's own header on the file, narrows it). Warnings marked there_at_our_first_read were issued before we began reading (11 November 2026, 02:2x UTC): their earlier history is in incidents/2026-11-10-storm-charles/data/weather/warnings.json (incident.meteorologist@). Times of the windows are as IPMA writes them (no zone; Lisbon and Madeira are on UTC in November, the Azores on UTC-1).
label: fact: IPMA's values, reshaped by us; computed fields say so
window_zone: start_utc and end_utc are start and end with Z appended: our reading, not IPMA's statement. IPMA writes no zone on a warning's window; its documentation says forecast times are UTC and says nothing for warnings. On the mainland and Madeira in winter local time is UTC, so nothing turns on it there; for the Azores (AOR, ACE, AOC) the window may be local time (UTC-1): unconfirmed.
